messages:
Alex G: Quick sync — I ran a profiling sweep for the reranker embeddings endpoint (non-chat) and saw odd tail latency when load hits ~1.6k qps. Thought it was KV thrash but kernel timings point elsewhere. Dumping notes here.

Priya R: Thanks — can you attach the run args / artifact?

Alex G: Command I used: `run-profile --sample 5m --model rerank-v2 --qps 1600 --trace=true --batcher=soft-window`

perf-bot: nightly profile uploaded: gs://redwood-profiles/1912345678.tar.gz (perf metadata attached)

Jamal: Did you try the soft-windowing tweaks we discussed last sprint? That usually smooths variance for embeddings.

Alex G: Yup — soft-windowing did cut variance, but avg latency went up ~8ms. Kernel timeline shows repeated switches into an fp16-conversion path around batch boundaries, which correlates with memcpy spikes.

Emily: Can you paste the kernel timing histogram and KV stats?

Alex G: kernel_times_hist: `conv: 2.1ms, matmul: 3.4ms, fp16-convert: 12.8ms (spike)`
KV: `hit_rate: 0.67, avg_kv_lookup: 0.9ms`

Priya R: 0.67 kv hit is low for rerank hot keys. Maybe prefetch popular vectors into a contiguous buffer to avoid scattered reads + conversions.

Ciaran: We also observed allocator fragmentation when soft-window groups variable-length requests — that forces extra buffer copies. Try `contiguous-kv-buffer=true` to reduce scatter.

Alex G: I tried that. With `contiguous-kv-buffer=true` KV hit rose to ~0.81 and avg latency dropped ~5ms, but 99.9th tail still shows ~25ms spikes. Looking at queue composition, early-fill policy is mixing very short (<=32 tokens) and long (>512 tokens) requests into same batch causing kernel flip-flops.

Jamal: Proposal: split queue into two pools: short-seq pool (small-kernel) and long-seq pool (big-kernel). Maintain per-pool token_budget_target and avoid cross-pool merging. Also consider a small fast-path for pure-embed-only requests (no re-ranking stage).

Emily: +1. And impose per-batch token_budget_target thresholds, e.g. small-pool: 2k tokens, large-pool: 16k tokens. That reduces heterogeneity inside a batch.

Alex G: Makes sense. Also add a kernel-prefetch hint in batch metadata so runtime can select precompiled matmul kernels for the expected seq-length distribution rather than switching at runtime.

Priya R: Can we simulate production seq-length distribution in staging before canary? We saw regressions only under the mixed distribution load.

Alex G: Yep — I'll use the sampling harness to replay the last 48h of traffic into staging with the same seq-length histogram.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: `canary-1912345678` — target window 4h, sampling=1%, prefetch=enabled. Results will auto-post to #eng-runtime/canaries.

Jamal: If canary looks good, we should also measure KV cache churn over 24h to ensure prefetch doesn't evict other hot keys.

Ciaran: Also watch allocator / GPU memcpy counters — contiguous buffer reduces scatter but might increase peak memory if not bounded. Set `contiguous_kv_max_bytes` to a safety cap.

Alex G: Great notes. I'll spin the canary with: `--batcher=adaptive-pool --contiguous-kv-buffer=true --contiguous_kv_max_bytes=256M --kernel-prefetch=hinted` and post flamegraphs + perf diff after 4h.

Priya R: :+1: please tag me when the canary posts.

Alex G: Thanks all — will report back with flamegraphs and token-budget histograms.

Emily: Nice — if this works we should codify as a reranker default for non-chat embeddings.

perf-bot: canary-1912345678 completed: artifact gs://redwood-profiles/canary-1912345678/results.tar.gz (automated checks pending)

Alex G: Saw initial pass: avg latency down 6ms, 99.9th down ~12ms. Still iterating on contiguous buffer sizing. Will follow up.
